exposure: Autologous erythrocyte transfusions during cesarean section
Allogeneic erythrocyte transfusions during cesarean section
outcome: intraoperative safety (assessed by urinalysis for hemoglobin, bilirubin, and urobilinogen)
cohort: The study included 27 parturient women with non-transfusion-dependent thalassemia who received erythrocyte transfusions during cesarean section.
finding: Both autologous and allogeneic erythrocyte transfusion strategies were found to be safe and effective for parturient women with non-transfusion-dependent thalassemia undergoing cesarean section, provided strict indications and standardized operating procedures were followed.
mod_finding: The study found both autologous and allogeneic erythrocyte transfusions to be safe and effective specifically when administered during cesarean section.
